ticket.title: The Gold chosen body is stored as the placeholder <filled> instead of the code
ticket.description:
Measured while proving the DPO shard end to end after GB-216. `hole_filler_dpo.parquet` now has 2 real rows with prompt/chosen/rejected columns, the scope signature (/tmp/gb-gold-crate/src/lib.rs::grapheme_count) and a genuinely rejected attempt containing `use unicode_segmentation::UnicodeSegmentation;`. The `chosen` column, though, reads `grapheme_count: <filled>` - the literal placeholder rather than the accepted code.

Same shape shows up upstream: the spool record filled_holes map has keys `grapheme_count` and `<filled>`, so the filled body never got attached to the hole it fills. Regex `mine-patterns` is affected too: with 2 examples it proposes a template `<filled>` with an empty typed-hole list, which is a degenerate pattern rather than a discovered one.

This is the difference between a shard that exists and a shard that trains: a DPO pair whose chosen side is a placeholder is unusable. Fix belongs where the trace is assembled (joiner fill - the hole name and the body are both known there) and should assert that filled_holes contains at least one non-placeholder body before spooling.

verification_receipt.summary: The Gold/Silver trace now carries the accepted body instead of the literal <filled>: the CLI was building filled_holes as (symbol, "<filled>") while FillOutcome::code - the validated candidate - sat unused beside it. Verified live: the spool record for the newest fill holds the full function body including its doc comment and the crate::text::grapheme_count delegation, and the exported sft shard contains that text rather than a placeholder. record_trace now refuses to spool a hole whose body is empty or the placeholder, naming the hole, because a corpus that silently accepts untrainable pairs only fails when someone trains on it. Found while proving this: verification was writing the bare candidate as the whole file, erasing every mod declaration, so a correct candidate delegating to crate::text failed with "cannot find text in the crate root"; it now splices exactly as --apply does. Also found the GB-213 fixture itself was false - its doc comment promised a crate::text helper that did not exist, which is why every earlier attempt reached for unicode_segmentation. Gate: clippy -D warnings, 32 tests, fmt green across three commits.
